title: Two Sum II Input Array Is Sorted
statement: You get a list of integers sorted from small to large, and a target. Find the two different positions whose values add up to the target. Exactly one pair exists. Return the positions counting from 1, smaller first. Use only a constant amount of extra memory.

example.caption: 2 + 15 = 17 is too big, so 15 is out. Then 2 + 11 = 13 is too big, so 11 is out. Then 2 + 7 = 9 matches.

idea.sentence: Because the list is sorted, the sum of the two ends tells you which end is useless. Too small means the left value can never work. Too big means the right value can never work.

jargon.plain: Two index variables that walk through the same list, here from opposite ends toward each other.
Values only go up as you move right. This is what lets one comparison rule out a whole value.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the sorted list, then the target, e.g. [2,7,11,15], 9

vars.meaning: number of integers in the list

rows.name: Hash map
rows.note: Works, but stores numbers. The problem asks for constant extra memory.

rows.name: Two pointers
rows.note: Each step moves one pointer one place. They meet after at most n steps.

fast.takeaway: Sorting is the hint. It turns every comparison into a safe decision, so no memory of past numbers is needed.

stages.title: Both ends
stages.note: l on the smallest value, r on the largest.

stages.title: Add the ends
stages.note: Compute the sum of the two values under the pointers.

stages.title: Too small: move l
stages.note: Even the largest value left is not enough for the value at l, so it can never be part of the answer. Move l right.

stages.title: Too big: move r
stages.note: Even the smallest value left is too much for the value at r, so it is out. Move r left.

stages.title: Equal: done
stages.note: The sum equals the target. Return both positions plus one.

edges.title: Smallest input
edges.why: Two values is the minimum. The first sum already matches.

edges.title: Zeros
edges.why: Two equal values may form the pair. Pointers sit on different positions, so each zero is used once.

edges.title: Negative numbers
edges.why: The argument still holds with negatives. Sorted order is all it needs.

edges.title: Pair of equals
edges.why: The two 2s add to 4. The answer needs two positions, not two distinct values.

gotchas.text: The positions in the answer start at 1, not 0. Add one when you return.
Use l < r, not l <= r. With l == r the pointers would use the same number twice.
Do not sort here. The input is already sorted, and Array.sort with no comparator sorts as text: 10 comes before 9.
Return nil for no answer and []int{l + 1, r + 1} otherwise. A nil slice and an empty one both have length 0, but they look different once encoded as JSON (null versus []).

recap.pattern: Two pointers: ends of a sorted list
recap.key: Sum the ends. Too small, drop the left one. Too big, drop the right one. Equal, done.
moves: Too small: l++. Too big: r--
